title: A correspondent at Beaupréau to Ségur, July 1583, BnF 500 de Colbert 401 f. 143 (a third key of the Navarre design)

documents.shelfmark: BnF 500 de Colbert 401 f. 143 (Gallica btv1b10035574w canvas 154)

plaintext.source: None found. George Lasry's saved decryptions of 15 Oct 2024 include f. 143 (unpublished; not seen here).

transcription.notes: --digits count (58 numeric tokens, 42 distinct); NOTES give 63 tokens including letter-written signs. Signed 'vostre tres humble et tres ... serviteur'; the clear text describes the cipher design.

system.summary: A numeric cipher of the same chancery design as the ff. 233 and f. 321 keys by the writer's own description ('lettres, syllabes, doubles, nulles ... Les noms sont en lettres et syllabes'), with different values; figures up to 156 and letter-written signs (Pa, a, H, L, I).
system.sibling_key: ff. 233 key (key A, segur) and Tomokiyo's f. 321 key (navarre1586): same design, neither fits f. 143.
system.notes: Different key from ff. 233/239/288v per NOTES (it does not decode with key_v4.json); too short for the structured annealers, whose floor for this design lies between about 120 and 460 tokens.

prior_solution.where: George Lasry's saved decryptions of 15 Oct 2024 cover ff. 143, 233, 239 and 288v (his note to the project, Oct 2026); unpublished; earlier reported 25 Sept 2026 as an independent 2024 solution.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Gallica IIIF fetched with a browser User-Agent.
f. 143 transcribed from the full-resolution image with the ff. 233/239/288v letters (ct_143.txt).

Identified f. 143 as a letter TO Ségur from a correspondent at Beaupréau (not the king), whose clear text describes the design (letters, syllables, doubles, nulls; names in letters and syllables), in a key different from ff. 233/239/288v.
Key A (key_v4.json) and the f. 321 key judged not to fit f. 143; at 58 numeric tokens it is below the method's floor (matched controls fail at f. 333's size, ~100 tokens), so no solver run.

Applied key A (key_v4.json) and the f. 321 key (key_321.json) to ct_143.txt: the f. 321 key gives nothing; key A gives a few French-looking fragments (ande efeire, faisi) inside non-French runs, so not the same key.
George Lasry specified that his saved decryptions of 15 Oct 2024 cover f. 143 as well as ff. 233, 239, 288v; unpublished, not seen.
Split from segur under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): f. 143 is in a different key; its own entry, attempted, not solved here. ct_143.txt moved here.

outcome.method_basis: The 1583 letter is in a third key of the Navarre design; at 58 numeric tokens it is too short for the structured annealers, and neither known key of the volume fits. George Lasry reports a 2024 decryption, unpublished.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Nothing of the cipher deciphered here; the clear text is transcribed in ct_143.txt.

gaps.item: the whole cipher of f. 143 (58 numeric tokens, letter-signs Pa, a, H, L, I, name codes 156, 134, 136)
gaps.detail: below the floor of the design-constrained annealer (controls fail at ~100 tokens); no other letter in this key in the volume; Lasry's 2024 decryption unpublished

outcome.notes: Attempted, not solved: transcribed and identified (a letter to Ségur from Beaupréau, July 1583, describing its own cipher), too short to attack. Lasry's saved decryption of 15 Oct 2024 covers it.

credits.note: saved decryption of f. 143 dated 15 Oct 2024, unpublished (his note of Oct 2026)
